terra.problem: The recipe punchline makes light of the serious sin of despising a husband and children.
The passage calls them Samaria's daughters but does not identify them as towns or say they live up a road.
Calling Damascus a city states a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
The claim that Tyre is a city to the north needs a reference outside this passage.
Calling Bethel a place in the Bible states a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
The claim about Babylon appearing often in the prophets needs a reference. The explanation also assumes what the baker was thinking.
The race punchline makes Jerusalem's serious sin the joke.
The verse does not say whether Jerusalem warned her sisters.
The text says Jerusalem will be ashamed, but does not say her pride is gone.
The punchline suggests looking down on someone works well until one's own turn comes, making light of scorn.
The passage does not say nobody was rescued in that day.
The casserole joke mentions a food other than cookies that is not in the passage or an answer on the card.
The verse says Jerusalem will remember and be ashamed when she receives her sisters. It does not say they are given as daughters right after she remembers.
The passage identifies Jerusalem's sins as the problem; it does not say comparing the sisters was the problem.
